newsitem.title: UK: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI READY TO CRASH PARTY.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI READY TO CRASH PARTY.

text.p: A tiny Texan with a 10-gallon smile suddenly looks ready to crash the party that Michelle Kwan and Chen Lu had planned to throw for themselves at next week's world figure skating championships in Lausanne.
The American and the Chinese waged a gold medal battle of epic proportions at last year's championships in Edmonton, Alberta, with Kwan edging the defending champion to take her first world title.
Until February it appeared they would write chapter two this month in a story likely to go on to include next year's Olympic Games in Japan.

Then up popped Tara Lipinski to take advantage of a surprising lapse by Kwan at the national championships where she upset her compatriot with a crowd-pleaser of a performance that included a triple loop-triple loop jump combination that no other skater in the world even attempts.
"I'm in shock." the tiny 14-year-old from Sugar Land, Texas said afterwards.

But she recovered well enough to deliver another dose of punishment to Kwan at the Championship Series finals in Hamilton, Ontario, two weeks later, inflicting a second successive defeat on a skater who until the nationals had won her last 11 competitions.
Next week Lipinski can complete a hat trick, which would be a huge advance for a skater who placed 15th in her first world championship a year ago.
She seems unflustered at the prospect. "It would be very hard to win but I don't feel much pressure going in. I can only get better," she said this week.
Kwan, meanwhile, must pick up the pieces from her two defeats and, at 16, re-establish herself as the gold medal favourite.
Chen's form is a mystery at the moment for she did not take part in any of the six Championship Series events leading up to the final.

But the elegant Chinese has the style and the jumping ability to win again, as she proved last year when she gave a performance that in any other year would have almost certainly been enough for gold.

Last year's bronze medallist, Russia's European champion Irina Slutskaya, is the main threat to the other three. The field which is likely to comprise more than 40 skaters will be cut to the low 30s in Monday's qualifying for the main event.

The men's championship, for which qualifying is on Sunday, looks likely to produce a victory for former champion Elvis Stojko of Canada following his sensational quadruple-triple jump en route to winning the Champions Series title.
Stojko lost the title he had won the previous two years when he missed his short programme combination last year in Edmonton but he seems to have put that behind him.

He will again come under threat from the Russians, with Olympic and European champion Alexei Urmanov, former European champion Ilya Kulik and Alexei Yagudin all in the chase. Urmanov and Kulik also produced quadruples in Hamilton though without the triple jump tacked on the end.
However there is a doubt about defending champion Todd Eldredge, as the American sustained an ankle injury in training last week.
He plans to compete but the injury has virtually ruled out the quad he was planning for the event.
Flamboyant Frenchman Philippe Candeloro has withdrawn because of a troublesome ankle injury.
The dance and pairs could both go to Russia, who have Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov ready to defend their ice dance title against team mates Anjekila Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov.
Krylova and her partner were beaten in the Champions Series final by Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz, who along with two French couples should battle for medals.
In pairs, Russia has former world and Olympic champion Artur Dmitriev with new partner Oksana Kazakova.
They made their case for a recall by beating world and European champions Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov at the Champions Series final.
But the winners there, Germans Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer, are the favourites in Lausanne.
